title: Rumors, Myths and Truths Behind Obama's Health Care Plan
summary: Third episode of a four-part Stuff You Should Know healthcare reform series, with guest Molly Edmonds, examining rumors, myths and truths about Obama's 2009 health care plan. Topics include whether the US can afford reform, paying for the plan and deficit neutrality, the uninsured as a hidden tax on insured families, higher taxes on high earners, "death panels" and end-of-life counseling, Medicare cuts and bundled payments with accountable organizations, rationing and the UK's NICE cost-effectiveness panels, innovation and drug marketing, abortion coverage in the House and Senate Finance bills, whether you can keep your current plan, socialized medicine and single payer fears, the public option, and whether illegal immigrants would be covered. The hosts also discuss chronic disease as a driver of costs, with Dr. Michael Roizen of the Cleveland Clinic.
topics: health care costs as share of GDP

entities.name: National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE)

segments.title: Opening and framing the myths episode
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode as part three of a four-part healthcare reform series, with Molly Edmonds joining, and preview covering myths from both left and right.

segments.title: Can the US afford health care reform?
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the claim that the US cannot afford reform, noting about 2.4 trillion dollars in annual spending, about a sixth of GDP, more than defense, and that the plan's specifics on paying for it are still being worked out.

segments.title: Paying for the uninsured and the hidden tax
segments.summary: The hosts explain that uninsured patients who use emergency care shift costs to insured families, estimated at about 1,000 dollars per family and 4 dollars per individual in premiums, and that the plan could reduce that cost-shifting.

segments.title: Taxes on high earners
segments.summary: Discussion of whether people earning over a quarter million dollars a year would face higher taxes, with the president's stated preference being to tax those earning above a set threshold, and the claim that these groups received breaks in prior years.

segments.title: Death panels myth and end-of-life counseling
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the House bill provision concerns voluntary end-of-life counseling reimbursed by Medicare and Medicaid, not mandatory termination or death panels. They discuss Betsy McCaughey's role in popularizing the term, John Stewart's interview, and AARP's support for the provision.

segments.title: Medicare cuts and bundled payments
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the claim that Medicare will not be affected, noting the president's promise of unchanged benefits but likely Medicare cuts to fund reform. They describe bundled services and accountable organizations, drawing on an interview with Dr. Michael Roizen of the Cleveland Clinic on paying for outcomes and prevention.

segments.title: Rationing health care and the UK NICE panel
segments.summary: The hosts explain the fear of rationing and compare with Britain's NICE, which uses quality-adjusted life years and a cost threshold of about 45,000 dollars a year. They state that nothing in the bills creates a similar panel that denies treatments, and that cost-effectiveness panels only assess which treatments work.

segments.title: Innovation, drug marketing and rationing by insurers
segments.summary: Discussion of whether proof-of-effectiveness panels would stifle innovation, with the view that drug companies might spend more on research than marketing. The hosts also note that insurers already ration through annual limits, lifetime maximums and pre-existing condition denials, and that patients and doctors both have incentives for more care.

segments.title: Abortion coverage in the reform bills
segments.summary: The hosts describe how the House bill and Senate Finance Committee chairman's mark handle abortion coverage: plans may offer it only with segregated private premiums, with federal funds limited to cases of rape, incest, or endangerment to the woman's life. Plans with and without abortion coverage would be offered side by side at the same price.

segments.title: Keeping your current insurance plan
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the president's promise that people can keep their plan, noting the plan will change to add consumer protections and that existing plans may have about five years to be grandfathered before competition may force changes.

segments.title: Socialized medicine, single payer, and the public option
segments.summary: The hosts define socialized medicine and single payer, arguing the proposals do not move toward either, and discuss fears that the public option would drive private insurers out. They note that co-ops were in the Senate Finance bill and that the public option is too uncertain to judge.

segments.title: Illegal immigrants and coverage
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether illegal immigrants would be covered. Children born in the US would be covered as citizens, but undocumented adults would not receive subsidies due to proof requirements, though they could still buy insurance in the exchange.

segments.title: Closing and preview of next episode
segments.summary: The hosts thank Molly Edmonds, preview the fourth episode on health care systems around the world, and point listeners to HowStuffWorks for more on healthcare reform.
